name: RNA Extraction
description: TRIzol (phenol-chloroform) based total RNA extraction from cells or tissue. Work in an RNase-free environment throughout. Suitable for downstream RT-qPCR, RNA-seq, or Northern blotting.
source_note: General educational template based on Chomczynski-Sacchi acid guanidinium thiocyanate-phenol-chloroform method.

steps.title: Lyse sample in TRIzol
steps.description: Add TRIzol directly to cell monolayer or tissue. For cells: aspirate media, add TRIzol, pass lysate through pipette tip several times. For tissue: homogenize in TRIzol with rotor-stator or pestle.
steps.notes: Ensure complete homogenization. Incubate at RT for 5 min to allow nucleoprotein complex dissociation.
steps.warnings: TRIzol contains phenol — toxic and corrosive. Work in fume hood. Wear gloves, lab coat, and eye protection.

steps.title: Add chloroform and mix
steps.description: Add chloroform, cap tubes, and shake vigorously by hand for 15 seconds. Do not vortex. The mixture will turn milky.
steps.notes: Do not vortex — gentle manual shaking gives cleaner phase separation.
steps.warnings: Chloroform is toxic and volatile. Handle in fume hood only.

steps.title: Centrifuge for phase separation
steps.description: Centrifuge to separate the mixture into three phases: lower red phenol-chloroform organic phase (contains DNA/protein), white interphase (contains DNA/protein), and upper aqueous phase (contains RNA).
steps.notes: The aqueous (top) phase contains ~60% of total RNA. Aqueous phase volume is ~600 µL from 1 mL TRIzol.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase
steps.description: Carefully aspirate only the clear upper aqueous phase into a fresh RNase-free tube. Avoid disturbing the white interphase or lower organic phase.
steps.notes: Take slightly less volume (~500 µL) to ensure no organic phase contamination. Tilt tube at angle if needed.
steps.warnings: Interphase/organic phase contamination will compromise RNA quality.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA with isopropanol
steps.description: Add isopropanol to the aqueous phase. Mix by inverting 6–8 times. Incubate to precipitate RNA.
steps.temperature: RT or −20°C for 1 h for low-yield samples
steps.notes: For low-yield samples, precipitation at −20°C for 30 min to 1 h improves yield.

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet RNA
steps.description: Centrifuge to pellet the RNA. The pellet may be white or translucent and may be difficult to see.
steps.notes: Pellet will be on the side/bottom of tube. Mark tube orientation before centrifugation.

steps.title: Wash RNA pellet with 75% ethanol
steps.description: Carefully remove isopropanol supernatant. Add 75% ethanol (in DEPC-treated or nuclease-free water) to wash the pellet. Vortex briefly and centrifuge.
steps.notes: 75% ethanol removes remaining salt impurities. Repeat wash step if purity is critical.

steps.title: Air-dry RNA pellet
steps.description: Remove all ethanol without disturbing the pellet. Open tubes and allow to air-dry for ~5–10 min. Do not over-dry as this will greatly decrease RNA solubility.
steps.notes: Pellet is ready when all visible ethanol has evaporated and it looks slightly translucent. Do NOT use vacuum centrifuge — over-drying makes RNA difficult to dissolve.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA in nuclease-free water
steps.description: Add nuclease-free water (or DEPC-treated water) and incubate briefly at 55–60°C to aid dissolution. Pipette up and down to dissolve pellet.
equipment: Heat block or water bath at 55–60°C
steps.notes: Pipette up and down repeatedly to fully dissolve RNA. Store at −80°C; avoid repeated freeze-thaw.
steps.warnings: RNA is highly susceptible to RNase degradation. Keep on ice and work quickly.

steps.title: Quantify and assess RNA quality
steps.description: Measure RNA concentration (A260) and purity (A260/A280 ≥2.0; A260/A230 ≥1.8) with a spectrophotometer. Optionally run on Bioanalyzer or gel to check RNA integrity.
steps.notes: RIN (RNA Integrity Number) ≥ 7 is generally required for RNA-seq. Contamination with DNA can be removed by DNase I treatment.
